Types of Mixtures: A mixture contains two or more substances that are not chemically combined. In a solution the particles are very small, evenly spread, do not settle and do not scatter light; salt water is an example. In a colloid the particles are larger, do not settle and scatter light, which is the Tyndall effect; milk, fog and gelatin are colloids. In a suspension the particles are large, visible and settle out if left standing; muddy water is a suspension. A mixture can be separated by physical methods because the parts keep their own properties.
Solutions: Solute and Solvent: A solution is a homogeneous mixture in which a solute is dissolved in a solvent. The solvent is the substance present in the larger amount and does the dissolving; in salt water the solvent is water and the solute is salt. Water is called the universal solvent because it dissolves many substances. Solutions can be solid, liquid or gas, such as brass, sea water and air. Dissolving is a physical change: the solute particles spread between the solvent particles and can be recovered by evaporation. Like dissolves like: polar solvents such as water dissolve polar and ionic solutes, while nonpolar solvents dissolve nonpolar solutes such as oil.
Solubility: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a given temperature. A saturated solution holds all the solute it can; an unsaturated solution can still dissolve more; a supersaturated solution holds more than normal and can crystallize suddenly. For most solids solubility increases with temperature. For gases solubility decreases with temperature and increases with pressure, which is why warm soda goes flat. The rate of dissolving increases with stirring, higher temperature and smaller particle size (more surface area). A solubility curve graphs solubility against temperature.
Concentration: Concentration tells how much solute is dissolved in a given amount of solution. A dilute solution has little solute and a concentrated solution has a lot. Mass percent is (mass of solute / mass of solution) x 100%. Concentration in grams per liter is the mass of solute divided by the volume of solution. Molarity (M) is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution, M = n / V. Moles are found from n = mass / molar mass. When a solution is diluted, the amount of solute stays the same, so M1 V1 = M2 V2.
Separating Mixtures: Mixtures are separated by physical methods that use differences in properties. Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid using particle size. Evaporation separates a dissolved solid from its solvent. Distillation separates liquids with different boiling points by boiling and condensing the vapor. Chromatography separates substances such as dyes because they move at different rates through a material like paper. A magnet separates magnetic materials such as iron. A separating funnel separates liquids that do not mix, like oil and water. Several methods can be combined, for example a magnet, then adding water and filtering, then evaporating.
